scope: Every currently displayed Key Risks card in ordinary production HTML, metric. Selection and icon mapping are unit-independent. No PDF generation.

risks.label: APHID
risks.text: Blackfly and greenfly may gather on developing globe-artichoke flower heads.

risks.label: SLUGS AND SNAILS
risks.text: Young shoots are vulnerable to slugs and snails, which can shelter among old leaves.

risks.label: FROST DAMAGE
risks.text: Hard frost may cut leaves down, with regrowth appearing in spring.

risks.label: BOTRYTIS
risks.text: Grey mould can affect leaves and stalks in damp, stagnant conditions.

risks.label: SCLEROTINIA ROT
risks.text: Stem bases rot and may carry fluffy white mould with black, seed-like resting bodies.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs may nibble spring shoots; established Jerusalem artichokes usually outgrow light leaf damage.

risks.label: MICE
risks.text: Mice may burrow among tubers in winter and eat stored or unlifted roots.

risks.label: VIOLET ROOT ROT
risks.text: Purple fungal growth on roots, with yellowing and dying fern, can indicate violet root rot.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Young shoots may turn black and die if a severe frost occurs in late spring.

risks.label: PERENNIAL WEEDS
risks.text: Couch grass, bindweed and other perennial weeds are a serious long-term problem in asparagus beds.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Spears are gnawed, making them unfit for table use.

risks.label: RED SPIDER MITE
risks.text: Pale mottling appears on upper leaf surfaces, with tiny mites beneath.

risks.label: WHITEFLY
risks.text: Whitefly can weaken aubergines under glass.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs may chew young plants and fruit touching the soil.

risks.label: APHID
risks.text: Aphids gather on young leaves and shoots.

risks.label: Black Bean Aphid
risks.text: Black bean aphid clusters on the tender growing tips of broad beans, especially on spring-sown plants, and can also attack French beans in midsummer.

risks.label: Chocolate Spot
risks.text: Small chocolate-brown spots appear on leaves, with dark streaks along the stems; pods and seeds may also be marked.

risks.label: Pea and Bean Weevil
risks.text: Tell-tale signs are U-shaped notches around the edges of young pea or bean leaves, and sometimes damage to the growing centres.

risks.label: Birds
risks.text: Birds can be a nuisance in several ways.

crops.name: Bean, French
warnings: Page 2: content exceeds the layout budget by approximately 19 mm; check the exported PDF for spillover.

risks.label: Black Bean Aphid
risks.text: Black bean aphids can cluster on French-bean shoots in summer.

risks.label: No Pods
risks.text: French beans may drop flowers or set few pods when roots are dry, especially in hot weather.

risks.label: Pea and Bean Weevil
risks.text: Tell-tale signs are U-shaped notches around the edges of young pea or bean leaves, and sometimes damage to the growing centres.

risks.label: Birds
risks.text: Birds can be a nuisance in several ways.

risks.label: NO PODS
risks.text: Runner beans often fail to set pods when roots become dry, when weather is very hot and dry, or when pollinating insects are scarce.

risks.label: HALO BLIGHT
risks.text: Semi-transparent or water-soaked spots with yellow halos on leaves are a warning sign.

risks.label: Black Bean Aphid
risks.text: Black aphids can gather on soft runner-bean growth, leaving sticky honeydew and distorted leaves.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs are the chief pest of young runner bean plants, especially in cool, wet weather while growth is slow.

risks.label: Slugs
risks.text: Leaf beet is usually hardy and trouble-free, but slugs may nibble young plants, especially in autumn or damp weather.

risks.label: Manganese Deficiency
risks.text: Yellowing between leaf veins can indicate a nutrient problem, but symptoms overlap.

risks.label: Leaf Spot
risks.text: Leaf spots may have pale brown centres and dark brown or purple margins, roughly 6 mm across.

risks.label: Bolting
risks.text: Plants sometimes run to seed before roots have developed.

risks.label: Fanging
risks.text: Forked roots are usually caused by adding fresh manure shortly before sowing.

risks.label: Mangold Fly (Leaf Miner)
risks.text: Small white grubs burrow inside the leaves, causing tunnels which later turn into blisters.

risks.label: Heart Rot
risks.text: Leaves wilt in summer and the tops of the roots develop brown, sunken patches.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Summer and autumn broccoli is very prone to caterpillar damage.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Club root causes swollen, distorted roots, poor growth and wilting in warm weather.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Sprouting broccoli is winter-hardy, but severe frost can damage shoots.

risks.label: PIGEONS
risks.text: Pigeons can strip young plants and winter crops.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Club root causes swollen, distorted roots, poor growth and wilting in warm weather.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Cabbage white butterfly and moth caterpillars chew leaves and may shelter among developing sprouts.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs can damage young plants and older sprouts, especially in wet weather.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Extreme frost can damage older sprouts.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Club root causes swollen, distorted roots, poor growth and wilting in warm weather.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Caterpillars of cabbage white butterfly, cabbage moth and related pests chew holes in leaves and may burrow into cabbage hearts.

risks.label: Cabbage Root Fly
risks.text: Cabbage root fly larvae tunnel into roots and stem bases.

risks.label: Pigeons
risks.text: Pigeons strip soft leaf tissue from cabbage and other brassicas, often leaving stalks and veins.

risks.label: POOR FRUIT SET
risks.text: Flowers may fail to set during cold, excessive heat or drought.

risks.label: RED SPIDER MITE
risks.text: Sweet peppers can develop pale mottling and bronzing when red spider mites feed beneath leaves.

risks.label: BLOSSOM END ROT
risks.text: Brown patches appear at the bottom of the fruit - a frequent problem where growing bags are used.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs may damage young plants and late, slow-ripening fruit near the soil surface.

risks.label: Carrot Fly
risks.text: Tell-tale signs on carrots are reddish leaves which wilt in sunny weather and later turn yellow.

risks.label: Fanging
risks.text: Fanging is usually caused by adding manure or compost to the soil shortly before seed sowing.

risks.label: Small Roots
risks.text: Aphids and virus will stunt growth and reduce yield, but even in the absence of pests and diseases many gardeners produce disappointingly small carrots.

risks.label: Splitting
risks.text: Much more serious than fanging of carrots, because the roots will not store.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Club root causes swollen, distorted roots, poor growth and wilting in warm weather.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Caterpillars chew leaves and can hide in cauliflower curds.

risks.label: Cabbage Root Fly
risks.text: Cabbage root fly maggots tunnel into roots and stems.

risks.label: Button Cauliflowers
risks.text: Tiny premature heads can follow growth checks from drought, poor fertility, crowded or root-bound plants, transplant stress or pest damage.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs can damage seedlings and later chew holes in swollen roots.

risks.label: CARROT FLY
risks.text: Brown lines or tunnels across the lower part of the root may be caused by carrot root fly maggots.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Celeriac is hardy, but exposed roots and frozen ground can make winter harvesting difficult.

risks.label: Celery Fly (Leaf Miner)
risks.text: Celery leaf miner makes pale blotches that turn brown and papery.

risks.label: Bolting
risks.text: Bolting is a serious problem, especially in dry seasons or where young plants have been checked.

risks.label: Slugs and Snails
risks.text: Slugs and snails chew celery leaves and stems, especially in damp conditions.

risks.label: Celery Fly (Leaf Miner)
risks.text: Larvae mine celery leaves, making pale blotches that turn brown and papery.

risks.label: Celery Leaf Spot (Blight)
risks.text: Brown or yellowish-brown spots appear first on the outer leaflets and then spread to all of the foliage.

risks.label: Slugs
risks.text: Slugs can chew chicory seedlings and leaves, including beneath forcing or blanching covers.

risks.label: Bolting
risks.text: Cold conditions while young, drought or other growth checks can trigger premature flowering.

risks.label: Rotting
risks.text: Rot can develop in crowded, wet heads or roots under forcing covers.

risks.label: SOIL PESTS
risks.text: Cutworms and swift moth caterpillars can damage chicory seedlings or roots.

crops.name: Courgettes and Marrows
warnings: Page 1: content exceeds the layout budget by approximately 1 mm; check the exported PDF for spillover.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs chew seedlings and young plants, especially in cold, wet conditions.

risks.label: MILDEW
risks.text: Powdery mildew produces a white coating on leaves, often late in the season.

risks.label: POOR POLLINATION
risks.text: If fruitlets yellow, wither or fail to swell, pollination may be poor.

risks.label: FRUIT ROT
risks.text: Fruit resting on wet soil may soften and rot.

risks.label: RED SPIDER MITE
risks.text: Speckled, yellowing leaves and fine webbing underneath can indicate red spider mite.

risks.label: BITTERNESS
risks.text: Stress, including uneven moisture or temperature, can increase bitterness.

risks.label: MILDEW
risks.text: Powdery mildew often appears on older leaves later in the season.

risks.label: LACK OF WARMTH
risks.text: Cold sowing or planting conditions check growth and can give slugs, woodlice and soil diseases a chance to damage young plants.

risks.label: MILDEW
risks.text: Powdery mildew often appears on older leaves later in the season.

risks.label: Slugs and Snails
risks.text: Slugs and snails may chew seedlings and low fruit.

risks.label: LACK OF WARMTH
risks.text: If sowing or planting conditions are cold, plants grow slowly and become easy prey for slugs, woodlice and damping-off diseases.

risks.label: CUCUMBER MOSAIC VIRUS
risks.text: Cucumber mosaic virus can cause mottled, puckered leaves, stunting and distorted fruit.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs can damage seedlings and blanched endive hearts in cool, damp weather.

risks.label: BOLTING
risks.text: Cold while young, drought and other growth checks can cause endive to flower prematurely.

risks.label: ROTTING
risks.text: Pale hearts can rot quickly in damp conditions.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Hard frost can damage hearts.

risks.label: BOLTING OR STEMMY BULBS
risks.text: Cold while young, drought and root disturbance can trigger premature flowering.

risks.label: SMALL OR DRY BULBS
risks.text: Drought and poor fertility produce small, less juicy bulbs.

risks.label: LOWER SHEATH ROT
risks.text: Lower sheaths may soften and decay.

risks.label: FROST
risks.text: Hard frost damages bulbs.

risks.label: WHITE ROT
risks.text: White rot affects onions, shallots, garlic and leeks.

risks.label: Allium Leaf Miner
risks.text: Adult flies make distinctive rows of small white feeding punctures on allium leaves.

risks.label: RUST
risks.text: Orange pustules appear on allium leaves, especially leeks and garlic.

risks.label: BIRDS OR FROST LIFTING CLOVES
risks.text: Shallow cloves may be pulled by birds or lifted by frost.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Caterpillars of cabbage white butterfly, cabbage moth and related pests chew holes in leaves.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Swollen, distorted roots cause poor growth and wilting in sunshine.

risks.label: Cabbage Whitefly
risks.text: Small white-winged insects and scale-like young live below brassica leaves; adults fly up when disturbed.

risks.label: Mealy Aphid
risks.text: Large clusters of waxy, greyish 'greenflies' occur on the underside of leaves and tips of plants from June onwards in hot, dry weather.

risks.label: Woody Kohl Rabi
risks.text: Drought, growth checks, crowding or delayed harvesting make the swollen stem hard and fibrous.

risks.label: Flea Beetle
risks.text: Tiny jumping beetles chew small round holes in young leaves, especially in warm dry weather.

risks.label: Cabbage Caterpillars
risks.text: Caterpillars of cabbage white butterfly, cabbage moth and related pests chew holes in leaves.

risks.label: Club Root (Finger and Toe)
risks.text: Swollen, distorted roots cause poor growth and wilting in sunshine.

risks.label: White Rot (Mouldy Nose)
risks.text: White rot affects onions, shallots, garlic and leeks.

risks.label: Allium Leaf Miner
risks.text: Adult flies make distinctive rows of small white feeding punctures on allium leaves.

risks.label: Leek Moth
risks.text: Small creamy-white to pale green caterpillars with brown heads and small legs feed within young leek and onion leaves, producing translucent patches, shredded foliage and sometimes secondary rot.

risks.label: Rust
risks.text: Orange pustules appear on allium leaves, especially leeks and garlic.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Keep soil clean of weeds, start with strong plants, patrol at dusk or dawn, and avoid sowing or planting when soil is bare for too short a time for slugs to disperse.

risks.label: ROOT APHID
risks.text: Plants may suddenly wilt and die as soil-dwelling aphids attack roots.

risks.label: Bolting
risks.text: Lettuces produce thick flowering stems if left in the soil after hearts have formed.

risks.label: Downy Mildew
risks.text: Older leaves, especially in damp autumn weather, may develop mildew.

crops.name: Mushroom
warnings: sowing_notes: automatic fallback selection; prepare a coordinated editorial extract before approval.

risks.label: PESTS
risks.text: Mushroom flies can infest compost and damage developing mushrooms.

risks.label: Contaminating moulds
risks.text: Contaminating fungi can discolour mushroom substrate or distort and decay developing mushrooms.

risks.label: Poor cropping
risks.text: Slow colonisation or stalled cropping may result from unsuitable temperatures, moisture or ventilation.

risks.label: White Rot (Mouldy Nose)
risks.text: White rot affects onions, shallots, garlic and leeks.

risks.label: Allium Leaf Miner
risks.text: Adult flies make distinctive rows of small white feeding punctures on allium leaves.

risks.label: Bolting
risks.text: Prolonged cold can trigger premature flowering, especially in large sets or young plants checked by weather.

risks.label: Leek Moth
risks.text: Leek-moth caterpillars can mine onion and shallot leaves and damage bulbs.

risks.label: FLEA BEETLE
risks.text: Flea beetles make small round holes in young brassica leaves, especially during warm, dry weather.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs chew leaves and seedlings, especially pak choi in damp conditions.

risks.label: BOLTING
risks.text: Cold checks, long days, heat or drought can encourage premature flowering, depending on the species and variety.

risks.label: CABBAGE CATERPILLARS
risks.text: Chinese cabbage and other brassica leaves may be attacked by caterpillars.

risks.label: CANKER
risks.text: In wet winters, heavy soils, acid soil or ground containing fresh manure, the tops of roots may develop brown or black fungal rot.

risks.label: POOR GERMINATION
risks.text: Parsnip seed loses viability quickly.

risks.label: CARROT ROOT FLY
risks.text: Carrot root fly may visit parsnips.

risks.label: Splitting
risks.text: Much more serious than fanging of carrots, because the roots will not store.

risks.label: PEA MOTH / CATERPILLARS
risks.text: The most obvious pea problem is caterpillars inside pods, eating the peas.

risks.label: MILDEW
risks.text: Mildew often appears from about the second week of July onwards, especially on late sowings or in damp, muggy weather.

risks.label: BIRDS
risks.text: Birds eat seed and seedlings and may peck leaves.

risks.label: MICE
risks.text: Mice may take the large edible seeds before germination.

risks.label: BLIGHT
risks.text: Potato blight spreads rapidly in warm, wet weather, causing brown foliage lesions, collapse and potentially tuber decay.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs tunnel into tubers, particularly in damp soil or beneath covers and mulches.

risks.label: SCAB
risks.text: Common scab causes corky skin patches and is favoured by dry conditions as tubers form, particularly in alkaline soil.

risks.label: EELWORM
risks.text: Potato cyst nematodes can build up where potatoes are grown repeatedly.

risks.label: Woody, Hollow or Soft Radish Roots
risks.text: Summer radishes quickly become too hot, woody, hollow or soft if growth is checked or if they are left too long after reaching edible size.

risks.label: Checked Growth / Poor Root Quality
risks.text: Turnips, swedes and radishes need steady, quick growth.

risks.label: FLEA BEETLE
risks.text: Tiny beetles pepper seedling leaves with holes and can check young crops.

risks.label: BOLTING
risks.text: Winter radishes such as China Rose and Minowase should not be sown before July because early sowing can make them bolt instead of forming usable roots.

risks.label: CROWN ROT
risks.text: Decay at the crown can cause weak, dull stems and rotting buds.

risks.label: SLUGS UNDER FORCING POTS
risks.text: Slugs may hide inside forcing pots or buckets and damage the tender forced stems.

risks.label: POOR GROWTH OR STRINGY STEMS
risks.text: Usually linked to dry soil, lack of organic matter, overcropping, or forcing the same crown too often.

risks.label: HONEY FUNGUS
risks.text: Honey fungus can cause rhubarb crowns to decline and die.

risks.label: WHITE BLISTER
risks.text: Pale spots develop white spore pustules, often beneath the leaves.

risks.label: FORKED ROOTS
risks.text: Stones, compaction, fresh manure and damage to the young taproot can cause forking.

risks.label: SNAPPED ROOTS
risks.text: Long, brittle roots break when pulled against firm or sticky soil.

risks.label: BOLTING
risks.text: Premature flowering can reduce the root crop.

risks.label: BOLTING
risks.text: Heat, long days and dry soil can trigger flowering.

risks.label: MOULD OR DOWNY MILDEW
risks.text: Yellow upper-leaf patches with grey-purple mould below can indicate downy mildew.

risks.label: NEW ZEALAND SPINACH FROST
risks.text: New Zealand spinach is frost-tender.

risks.label: MANGANESE DEFICIENCY
risks.text: Yellowing between veins can have several causes.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs attack seedlings and young plants, especially in cold wet conditions, and may damage fruit resting on the soil.

risks.label: MILDEW
risks.text: Powdery mildew produces a white coating on leaves, often late in the season.

risks.label: STEM DAMAGE AND ROT
risks.text: A broken stalk or damaged skin provides an entry point for storage rot.

risks.label: No Fruit
risks.text: Poor pollination can leave flowers without developing fruit, especially in cool weather.

risks.label: FLEA BEETLE
risks.text: Young swede seedlings may be peppered with small holes.

risks.label: Checked Growth / Poor Root Quality
risks.text: Turnips, swedes and radishes need steady, quick growth.

risks.label: CABBAGE ROOT FLY
risks.text: Maggots may tunnel roots.

risks.label: QUALITY PROBLEMS
risks.text: Dryness, crowding, hot weather or delayed harvesting can make roots smaller, harder or fibrous.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs damage young plants most when cold or wet conditions slow growth.

risks.label: COLD CHECK
risks.text: Cold soil and weather slow growth and nutrient uptake; seedlings may turn yellow and stall.

risks.label: POOR POLLINATION
risks.text: Gaps in full-sized cobs commonly result from poor pollination.

risks.label: CROSS POLLINATION
risks.text: Pollen from maize or different sweet-corn types can reduce the sweetness or tenderness of supersweet cobs.

risks.label: BLIGHT
risks.text: Tomato blight causes brown lesions on leaves and stems, followed by fruit decay and plant collapse in favourable damp conditions.

risks.label: Greenhouse Whitefly
risks.text: Whitefly adults and immature stages suck sap; sticky honeydew can support black sooty mould.

risks.label: Blossom End Rot
risks.text: A dark, leathery patch at the flower end of the fruit results from insufficient calcium reaching developing tissue, often because root moisture fluctuates.

risks.label: SPLIT FRUIT
risks.text: Irregular watering, particularly soaking after severe drying, can split ripe fruit.

risks.label: BLIGHT
risks.text: Blight causes rapidly spreading brown leaf and stem lesions and fruit decay in damp weather.

risks.label: Blossom End Rot
risks.text: A dark, leathery patch at the flower end of the fruit results from insufficient calcium reaching developing tissue, often because root moisture fluctuates.

risks.label: SLUGS
risks.text: Slugs chew low-hanging fruit, particularly on bush plants.

risks.label: SPLIT FRUIT
risks.text: Ripe fruit may split after irregular watering or rain following dry soil.

risks.label: FLEA BEETLE
risks.text: Late spring and early summer sowings can be badly peppered by flea beetle.

risks.label: Checked Growth / Poor Root Quality
risks.text: Turnips, swedes and radishes need steady, quick growth.

risks.label: CABBAGE ROOT FLY
risks.text: Maggots tunnel the roots.

risks.label: WOODY ROOTS
risks.text: Heat, drought, overcrowding, starvation or leaving spring roots too long makes roots woody, fibrous or strong-tasting.
